```{r}
##Growth in PALM scheme 
##Drop in Tonga's scheme 
df <- data.frame(
  place <- c("Total", "Tonga"),
  `2022` <- c(26185, 6035),
  `2024` <- c(30705, 3175)
)

theme_set(theme_classic())
colnames(df)<- c("Place","2022", "2025")
left_label <- paste(df$Place, round(df$`2022`),sep=", ")
right_label <- paste(df$Place, round(df$`2025`),sep=", ")
df$class <- ifelse((df$`2025` - df$`2022`) < 0, "red", "green")

# Plot
p <- ggplot(df) + geom_segment(aes(x=1, xend=2, y=`2022`, yend=`2025`, col=class), size=.75, show.legend=F) + 
                  geom_vline(xintercept=1, linetype="dashed", size=.1) + 
                  geom_vline(xintercept=2, linetype="dashed", size=.1) +
                  scale_color_manual(labels = c("Up", "Down"), 
                                     values = c("green"="#00ba38", "red"="#f8766d")) +  # color of lines
                  labs(x="", y="Workers (PALM)") +  # Axis labels
                  xlim(.5, 2.5) + ylim(0,1.1*((max(df$`2022`, df$`2025`))))  # X and Y axis limits

# Add text
p <- p + geom_text(label=left_label, y=df$`2022`, x=rep(1, NROW(df)), hjust=1.1, size=3.5)
p <- p + geom_text(label=right_label, y=df$`2025`, x=rep(2, NROW(df)), hjust=-0.1, size=3.5)
p <- p + geom_text(label="Year 2022", x=1, y=1.1*(max(df$`2022`, df$`2025`)), hjust=1.2, size=5)  # title
p <- p + geom_text(label="Year 2025", x=2, y=1.1*(max(df$`2022`, df$`2025`)), hjust=-0.1, size=5)  # title

# Minify theme
p + theme(panel.background = element_blank(), 
           panel.grid = element_blank(),
           axis.ticks = element_blank(),
           axis.text.x = element_blank(),
           panel.border = element_blank(),
           plot.margin = unit(c(1,2,1,2), "cm"))
```

```{r}
PALM_long <- df %>%

library(lubridate)

#install.packages("zoo")
library(zoo)

PALM_long$Date <- as.Date(as.yearmon(PALM_long$Date, "%b-%y"))
# Plot
PALM_long%>%
  ggplot( aes(x=Date, y=Workers, group=Category, color=Category)) +
```

```{r}
tonga_data <- df_with_changes %>% 
  filter(Category == "Tonga") %>%
  mutate(Change_Type = ifelse(Monthly_Change > 0, "Increase", 
                             ifelse(Monthly_Change < 0, "Decrease", "No Change")))

ggplot(tonga_data, aes(x = Date, y = Workers)) +
  geom_line(color = "#1f77b4", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Change_Type), size = 3) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(!is.na(Monthly_Change), 
                              paste0(ifelse(Monthly_Change > 0, "+", ""), 
                                     Monthly_Change), "")),
            vjust = -1, size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Decrease" = "#d62728", 
                               "Increase" = "#2ca02c",
                               "No Change" = "#ff7f0e")) +
  labs(title = "Tonga PALM Workers: Monthly intake",
       subtitle = "Annotations show net monthly additions/losses",
       y = "Number of Workers",
       color = "Change Type") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))


```


```{r}

# Step 1: Create the data frame
rse_tonga <- data.frame(
  Financial_year = c("2007/08", "2008/09", "2009/10", "2010/11", "2011/12",
                    "2012/13", "2013/14", "2014/15", "2015/16", "2016/17",
                    "2017/18", "2018/19", "2019/20", "2020/21", "2021/22",
                    "2022/23", "2023/24", "2024/25"),
  RSE_workers = c(805, 1355, 1142, 1411, 1398, 1573, 1600, 1563, 1687, 1822, 1899, 2037, 1807, 826, 957, 1202, 1307, 1608)
)

# Step 2: Convert financial year to proper date format (using July as midpoint)
rse_tonga$Year <- as.numeric(substr(rse_tonga$Financial_year, 1, 4)) + 0.5

# Step 3: Create the trend plot
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(rse_tonga, aes(x = Year, y = RSE_workers)) +
  geom_line(color = "#2c7bb6", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(color = "#d7191c", size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Trend of Tongan Workers in NZ's RSE Scheme (2007-2025)",
       x = "Year",
       y = "Number of RSE Workers",
       caption = "Source: New Zealand RSE Scheme Data") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2007.5, 2024.5, by = 2),
                   labels = paste0(seq(2007, 2024, by = 2), "/", seq(2008, 2025, by = 2))) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())


```


```{r}

# Create the data frame
visa_data <- data.frame(
  Year = c("2005-06", "2006-07", "2007-08", "2008-09", "2009-10", 
           "2010-11", "2011-12", "2012-13", "2013-14", "2014-15",
           "2015-16", "2016-17", "2017-18", "2018-19", "2019-20",
           "2020-21", "2021-22", "2022-23", "2023-24"),
  Visas_417 = c(114693, 134993, 154339, 187907, 175746, 
               185480, 214644, 249231, 229378, 214830,
               195673, 191955, 185450, 180223, 122673,
               31207, 79896, 178306, 193922),
  Visas_462 = c(751, 1812, 3488, 6409, 7422, 
              7442, 8348, 9017, 10214, 11982,
              18910, 19056, 25006, 28813, 26576,
              8379, 17463, 46125, 40634),
  Grand_Total = c(115444, 136805, 157827, 194316, 183168,
                192922, 222992, 258248, 239592, 226812,
                214583, 211011, 210456, 209036, 149249,
                39586, 97359, 224431, 234556)
)

# Convert to long format for ggplot
library(tidyr)
visa_long <- pivot_longer(visa_data, 
                         cols = c(Visas_417, Visas_462),
                         names_to = "Visa_Type",
                         values_to = "Count")

# Create stacked bar plot
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(visa_long, aes(x = Year, y = Count, fill = Visa_Type)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#1f77b4", "#ff7f0e"),
                    labels = c("417 Visas", "462 Visas")) +
  labs(title = "Australian Working Holiday Visas (2005-2024)",
       subtitle = "Breakdown of 417 vs 462 Visa Types",
       x = "Financial Year",
       y = "Number of Visas Issued",
       fill = "Visa Type",
       caption = "Source: Australian Department of Home Affairs") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        legend.position = "top") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma)

# Optional: Save the plot
#ggsave("australia_working_holiday_visas.png", width = 12, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

```{r}

# Create the data frame
imputed_data <- data.frame(
  Year = c("2018-19", "2019-20", "2020-21", "2021-22", "2022-23", "2023-24"),
  Workers = c(36125, 27576, 28600, 7751, 14493, 27231)
)

# Create bar plot
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(imputed_data, aes(x = Year, y = Workers)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "#1f77b4", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::comma(Workers)), vjust = -0.5, size = 3.5) +
  labs(title = "Backpackers in Agriculture",
       x = "Financial Year",
       y = "Imputed Value",
       caption = "* workers") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())

# Optional: Save the plot
ggsave("imputed_values_plot.png", width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)

```
